output: The A3 Hindhead tunnel, the UK's longest land tunnel, offers driver advice on speed limits, closures and diversions, breakdowns, standstill traffic, and cycling restrictions.

National Geological Screening by RWM reviews the geology of England, Wales and Northern Ireland across 13 regions to assess its suitability for safely disposing of higher-activity radioactive waste in a Geological Disposal Facility.

The GOV.UK Operational Delivery Profession accessibility statement explains how accessible the site is, offers alternative formats and a reporting route for problems, describes the EHRC enforcement process, and says the site was tested for WCAG 2.1 AA compliance on 20 October 2019.

GOV.UK's LGBT advice page lists free support services for discrimination, hate crime, revenge porn, domestic abuse, trans and LGB health, young people, and emotional distress, plus links on gender recognition, marriage, and rights.

Agents writing to HMRC about Self Assessment, PAYE or Income Tax should use standard primary and secondary subject headings so the letter reaches the right team, and include the client's National Insurance number, Unique Taxpayer Reference or employer reference.

GOV.UK lists annual monitoring reports from regional aggregates working parties for 2020–2022, covering primary aggregates extraction, sales, supply and demand, plus marine, recycled and secondary aggregates, with older reports archived.

Charities can sell alcohol at events directly linked to their aims without paying tax on the profits, but other alcohol sales may be taxable, risky, or require a licence, and free alcohol must be kept separate from ticket prices.

Natural England inspects land after reports of wildlife, pet, or beneficial invertebrate deaths or injuries possibly linked to pesticides, under the Wildlife Incident Investigation Scheme, with investigations lasting 1 to 4 hours or longer if poisoning is indicated.

Individuals can challenge UK government decisions made on national security grounds, such as exclusion, refused citizenship, deportation or citizenship deprivation, by applying to the independent Special Immigration Appeals Commission within strict time limits.

Attractions and facilities accessed from Highways England-managed roads can apply for brown tourist signs by submitting an application form, paying a deposit, and allowing at least nine months, with the applicant bearing design and installation costs.

Applicants who have changed gender can use the SIA's confidential "sensitive applications" process to apply for, renew, or replace a licence by first emailing the SIA, then waiting for a reply before applying.

The Ministry of Defence offers apprenticeships from level 2 to level 7 for new recruits and existing staff, across armed forces and civilian roles in areas such as engineering, IT, finance and business administration.

The UK's Arab Partnership, a joint DFID and FCO initiative backed by £110 million over four years, supports Egypt, Tunisia, Jordan, Morocco and Libya in pursuing economic growth and political reform, as part of the G8's Deauville Partnership.

The Arab Partnership Fund supports projects in the Middle East and North Africa that build capable, inclusive institutions and promote stability, with 2015-16 funding focused on Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco and Mauritania (bidding now closed).

Councils must investigate artificial light complaints that could be a statutory nuisance, meaning they unreasonably and substantially interfere with enjoyment of premises or harm health, and can serve abatement notices, though exemptions apply to certain sites such as airports, prisons and defence premises.

Air Passenger Duty assessments can cover errors from the last 4 years (up to 20 in cases of fraud or dishonesty), with interest charged on underpaid duty, and penalties including fixed, geared and daily amounts, plus appeal rights.
HMRC warns that schemes claiming to avoid Income Tax on company winding-up distributions (phoenixism) do not work, are caught by anti-avoidance rules, and users should declare the income.

Students and parents should keep phones and smartwatches out of exam rooms, avoid sharing suspected leaked exam questions (reporting them instead), and check exam times, permitted equipment, and water bottle rules in advance.

Under the Compulsory Beef Labelling Scheme, non-compliant beef or veal must be removed from sale until correctly labelled or processed outside the scheme, and non-compliance can lead to enforcement action ranging from verbal advice to criminal prosecution.

Ofsted registers and inspects certain children's social care services (such as children's homes and fostering agencies) and inspects others (such as local authority children's services), with unannounced or notified inspections, published reports, and a complaints procedure.

The GOV.UK page lists downloadable British Antarctic Territory legislation, organised into administration, crime and justice, environment, immigration and customs, miscellaneous, and repealed ordinances.

The terms set out how users of BCMS systems (CTS Online, AMLS and LUIS) must keep login details secure, use the service lawfully, and handle uploaded and downloaded data, while BCMS aims to provide the service but is not liable for outages or data corruption and Crown copyright applies to site material.

The British Embassy in Vietnam invites project proposals for financial year 2017/18 on access to information (up to £25,000) and media environment capacity building (up to £25,000), with bids due by 31 May 2017.

The British Embassy in Vietnam invites bids of up to £40,000 (deadline 15 May 2017) for projects enhancing Vietnamese patients' access to safe, high-quality medicines by supporting implementation of the Pharmaceutical Law 2016.

The British Embassy in Hanoi invites bids by 5 July 2018 for a two-year, £30,000-per-year UK Vietnam Fund project to improve journalists' capacity and the media environment, promoting state transparency and accountability.

The Capital Markets Climate Initiative, established in 2010, is a UK public-private partnership with over 80 financial and policy participants that designs and tests instruments to mobilise private finance for low carbon and climate-resilient projects in developing countries.

Charities don't pay tax on trading profits that serve their primary purpose, on small non-primary trading below set turnover limits, or on profits passed from a subsidiary trading company, but must pay tax on other trading profits and register for VAT if trading income exceeds the threshold.

Guidance on choosing a charity legal structure (CIO, charitable company, unincorporated association or trust) based on whether the charity needs corporate status and a wider membership, with the governing document defining the structure.

The Clinical Services Unit, part of UKHSA's Virus Reference Department and a WHO Collaborating Centre, provides reference and diagnostic testing for viruses such as HIV, hepatitis, measles and parvovirus B19, plus syphilis and STI PCR tests, and lists referral forms and contact details.

Local planning authorities should support digital infrastructure rollout by planning for full fibre and 5G in Local Plans, engaging early with operators, and coordinating with highways departments, as set out in NPPF chapter 10 for England.

Controlled Foreign Company rules, which apply to accounting periods from 1 January 2013, are anti-avoidance provisions that charge UK corporate shareholders (holding at least 25%) on profits diverted from the UK to low-tax foreign companies, subject to exemptions.

Core competencies for regulators are a set of skills relevant to all regulators, covering context, risk assessment, understanding those regulated, planning, checking and supporting compliance, responding to non-compliance, and evaluation, reviewed regularly as roles change.

Since 1 April 2019, companies buying goodwill and relevant assets with qualifying intellectual property can claim fixed 6.5% yearly Corporation Tax relief, up to six times the IP cost, with restrictions still applying in other cases.

GOV.UK's criminal legal aid page lists the statutory regulations, Standard Crime Contracts (2010, 2017, 2022, 2025), guidance manuals, and application and claim forms for criminal legal aid. (29 words)

Deposits of any substance or object at sea, on the seabed or from British vessels abroad may need a marine licence, with exemptions, self-service options, strict limits on waste disposal (only certain materials allowed after risk assessment), and explosives requiring licences.

If a company fails to file its Company Tax Return by the deadline, HMRC may estimate the tax owed through a "determination," which must be paid immediately, plus penalties and interest, and can only be replaced by filing the late return.

Free Holocaust education CPD for trainee and state-funded secondary teachers in England includes courses, workshops, a masters module, classroom resources, and beacon school networks, booked via online accounts.

Local authorities are advised to create a digital infrastructure strategy, led by a senior digital champion, that facilitates network rollout, fosters provider partnerships, plans ahead, and aggregates public demand.
HMRC warns that PSC and LLP arrangements transferring PSC shares to avoid the disguised remuneration loan charge do not work, and users and promoters face penalties and enforcement action.
HMRC warns that schemes claiming to avoid the disguised remuneration loan charge do not work, are tax avoidance, and urges users to withdraw from them and settle their tax affairs.
Schemes promising to avoid the new disguised remuneration loan charge don't work, so users must repay the loan in full or settle with HMRC by 5 April 2019 to avoid it.

HMRC warns that disguised remuneration schemes using capital advances and offshore joint or mutual share ownership arrangements to avoid Income Tax and NICs do not work, will be challenged, and users should withdraw and settle their tax affairs.

Dourine is a notifiable disease affecting equids (not humans) that has never been recorded in Great Britain; it spreads through sexual contact, causes often-fatal symptoms such as fever and paralysis, and must be reported immediately if suspected.

Government Property Agency's DVS (the Valuation Office Agency's property advisory arm) offers valuations, surveys, asset management and property advice to central government, the NHS and wider public sector to improve estate efficiency and delivery of government priorities.

DVSA email alerts explain how to subscribe to topics such as learning to drive, MOTs, and the Highway Code by creating a password-protected account, manage or unsubscribe via the Preferences tab, and get help.

The Cambridge-based East of England public health laboratory provides a 7-day microbiology service covering molecular, bacteriology, virology, avian influenza, blood-borne virus, specialist virology and liquid TB testing, with turnaround times from 1 to 7 days.

Ebola survivors face a lifetime ban on gamete donation, while people who have been in active Ebola transmission areas must defer sperm donation or male fertility treatment for 2 years and egg donation or female fertility treatment for 6 months after leaving.

Marketing authorisation holders must submit educational materials and distribution plans for products with additional risk minimisation measures to the MHRA for approval before marketing, with assessment targeted within 18 calendar days.

Two government-funded projects, totalling £2.7 million and running from April 2019 to March 2021, are trialling smart meter load control to charge electric vehicles automatically at the cheapest, lowest-carbon times.

The Electricity Demand Reduction pilot tested whether projects delivering lasting peak-time electricity savings could compete for Capacity Market funding, running Phase II from June 2015 to December 2018 with £6 million available.

If you are unhappy with your energy supplier's response about your electricity meter readings, you can request a free independent on-site test of your meter, though you may be charged if it is found to be working correctly.

This GOV.UK page lists emergency contacts for healthcare professionals needing urgent public health advice: local UKHSA health protection teams for local matters, and national UKHSA numbers for infectious diseases, radiation, chemicals and poisons, with an emergency switchboard for unsure cases.

Industrial plants listed as Part A(1) installations must show the Environment Agency they meet energy efficiency standards, including BAT-based measures, energy management systems, and monitoring and reporting for those generating energy from fossil fuels.

Natural England may inspect land that is the subject of a screening request or unapproved activity on semi-natural or uncultivated land, assessing habitats and features like archaeology and landscape, then issuing a screening decision or taking enforcement action, including prosecution.
ERDF investments in England from 2007 to 2013 helped 25,932 new businesses start or relocate and created around 131,375 jobs, with project lists, case studies and annual reports provided.

The UK government page lists centrally managed agriculture programmes, including ASAP, AECF, CASA, GAFSP, IPC and LEGEND, which aim to boost smallholder farmers' incomes, food security, climate resilience and land governance in developing countries.

Exceptional Assistance Measures provide case-by-case, last-resort practical support, such as medical evacuation, medical expenses and repatriation, to British nationals affected by overseas terrorist attacks, but not to those travelling against FCDO advice.

UK export licensing policy for Burkina Faso, an ECOWAS member, bans licences for small arms, light weapons, components and ammunition unless the ECOWAS Commission grants an exception, and requires a licence for certain military goods in transit.

UK export policy bars licences for small arms, light weapons, components and ammunition to Niger, as an ECOWAS member, unless ECOWAS grants an exception, and transit through the UK for Niger still needs a licence.

UK export licensing policy for Nigeria, as an ECOWAS member, bans licences for small arms, light weapons, components and ammunition unless the ECOWAS Commission grants an exception, and military transit through the UK to Nigeria requires a licence.

The UK bars export licences for small arms, light weapons, components and ammunition to The Gambia, as an ECOWAS member, unless the ECOWAS Commission grants a moratorium exception, and transit through the UK for The Gambia also requires a licence.

Factorial RCTs let developers test several product elements at once, efficiently and rigorously, during development, but they assume no interaction between elements, which is often violated in digital health, so multi-arm designs may be better.

Employers exempt from HMRC's online payroll reporting include those providing care or support at home to a disabled, elderly or infirm family member or employer, and those with disabilities, no internet access, or inability to use online channels, who may apply to HMRC to file paper returns.

In England, the Environment Agency issues three flood levels: alert (flooding possible, prepare now), warning (flooding expected, act now), and severe warning (risk to life, act immediately), so check alerts and follow official advice.

HMRC sends follower notices and accelerated payment notices to people involved in tax avoidance schemes, requiring them to settle tax, pay disputed amounts, or face penalties, with appeals available only against penalties.

Gas bills may be high due to price rises, increased usage, a faulty boiler, or estimated readings; steps like cheaper tariffs, lower thermostats, and servicing can help, and faulty meters are rare but can be independently tested.

Employers or unions can ask the CAC to decide a bargaining method when they have agreed recognition voluntarily but cannot agree a method, or one party claims the other has not followed the agreed method, provided the recognition request was withdrawn after agreement.

Teachers from under-represented groups who work in state-funded English schools can join tailored leadership programmes, delivered September 2018 to July 2020 by schools funded through regional hub lead schools, often free of charge.

Charities and CASCs can claim tax back on donations using Gift Aid declarations, which donors may make on paper, online or verbally, must be kept for at least six years (or permanently for enduring declarations), and must include specified information, or HMRC may require repayment of the tax claimed.

Great crested newts and their eggs, breeding sites and resting places are legally protected, so harming or disturbing them is an offence unless covered by a Natural England licence, and pond work is best done in late autumn and winter when newts are least likely to be present.

Failing to provide non-domestic rent, lease or ownership details to the Valuation Office Agency incurs escalating penalties, capped at £500 or the property's rateable value, appealable within 28 days.

UK hydroelectric power supplies about 1.5% of electricity, mostly from large Scottish schemes, with limited large-scale growth possible but modest potential remaining for sustainable small-scale and micro-hydro projects, subject to planning, permits and certification.
Free Isaac Physics online resources, events and support help GCSE and A level students, and their teachers, move on to higher-level physics, with some events limited to eligible students.

The HIV and AIDS Reporting System (HARS) is a UKHSA-managed quarterly, pseudonymised patient-level dataset collected from over 160 NHS-funded specialist HIV services in England, covering people aged 15 and over, to improve surveillance, quality of care and commissioning.
HM Land Registry's Lender Services let lenders and their agents submit electronic discharges of charges, with access governed by a Memorandum of Understanding, applied for via Business e-services.

Guidance defining homelessness statistics terms, including statutory homelessness (priority need acceptances), rough sleeper definitions, temporary accommodation, and prevention and relief, plus the P1E quarterly return.

Household projections for England are derived by DCLG from ONS sub-national population figures, using household representative rates from censuses and Labour Force Survey data, with population change contributing about 98% of household growth.

Guidance for British nationals buying property in Tunisia covers legal advice, taxes, complaints, renting and selling, and stresses that non-Tunisians need Governor authorisation in residential areas, must use a local lawyer, and should have contracts checked before signing.

Anyone can request a review of a scheduled monument decision within 28 days of notification, on grounds such as significant evidence, factual error, process irregularity, or new evidence of national importance, with the Secretary of State having discretion.

Departments publish appointment letters for Government Major Projects Portfolio Senior Responsible Owners on a single standard transparency page, with letters listed alphabetically by project, following the Infrastructure and Projects Authority's guidance and the Osmotherly Rules commitment.

Departments must publish annual GOV.UK transparency data on non-consolidated performance related pay for SCS and delegated grades, using the Cabinet Office template, creating a new publication page per release, linking it on data.gov.uk, and adding it to the department's collection page.

Departments must prepare monthly workforce management data (with Cabinet Office guidance), then publish it via a standard GOV.UK transparency publication page, add links on data.gov.uk, and add the publication to their collection page.

Charity Commission guidance explains how to update your charity's details online, including trustees, the charity contact, public address, basic information and bank accounts, and which details are shown publicly on the register.
The page provides downloadable PDF documents setting out UK import tariff quotas for Ukrainian beef, cereals, dairy products, eggs, pigmeat and poultrymeat, each with accompanying annexes.

The IAPT payment approach is a local payment model for adult psychological therapy services that rewards providers for patient outcomes, adjusted for case complexity and activity levels, to encourage effective, consistent treatment.

The report helps NHS providers find ways to boost productivity in elective care, drawing on strong-performing ophthalmic and orthopaedic units at home and abroad, to ease budget and demand pressures while protecting quality.

A marine licence is required to incinerate any substance or object in English or Northern Irish offshore waters on a vehicle, vessel, marine structure or floating container, and for certain incineration or loading activities elsewhere at sea.

The UK Government's Industrial 5G Testbeds and Trials competition, funded via the £200 million 5GTT Programme, invites private-sector-led consortia (including an SME) to trial 5G industrial applications in manufacturing and logistics, with applications closing 10 October 2019.

Employees at companies with 50 or more staff can request information and consultation arrangements, with 2% of employees needed to make the request, and can apply to the Central Arbitration Committee (CAC) for confidentiality or dispute resolution.

Guidance for bereaved families of British nationals murdered, manslaughtered, or who died suspiciously in Barbados covers post-mortems, burial, cremation or repatriation, police and judicial processes (which can take years), the death penalty stance, media intrusion, and limited local support.

The Infrastructure and Projects Authority supports overseas governments, development banks and multilateral bodies with infrastructure advice, assurance, project structuring, PPP expertise and training, while supporting UK government objectives abroad.

Inland waterways vessels fall into three categories, passenger ships (over 12 passengers, governed by MSN 1823 or, for EU vessels, MSN 1824), non-passenger vessels (Class IX(A), per MGN 469), and pleasure boats (private, non-commercial use, per MGN 489), each with its own rules.

Insurance Premium Tax is a tax on general insurance premiums, charged at 12% standard or 20% higher rate, with various exemptions; insurers and certain intermediaries must register, file returns (usually quarterly), and keep records.

Lodge an agreed notice to protect a charge on a registered title via the HM Land Registry portal (e-AN1) by entering the title number, applicant, chargee and charge date, attaching supporting evidence, and paying the fee, with limitations requiring postal or DRS applications.

Use HM Land Registry's portal e-RX3 service to lodge an application to cancel a restriction on a title: enter the title number, applicant details, reason and supporting evidence, then submit and pay the fee (some applications need the Digital Registration Service or post instead).

Log in to the HM Land Registry portal, go to Administrative Services > Manage business unit, change the contact details to enter your collective email address, then set whether users may use alternative correspondence email addresses.
Log in to the HM Land Registry portal, enter a property's details under 'Enquiry by property description' to find its title number, view the register for a fee if needed, then log out.

PDFs from HM Land Registry portal applications are free to access for 90 days from registration completion, and this guide explains how to find them via the download categories, search filters, and business unit areas.

Users can reset a Land Registry portal password only after logging in once, by entering their User ID, choosing password reset, and answering their shared secret questions, with authorised users contacting their Business Unit Administrator and administrators contacting Customer Support if they cannot recall the answers.

Users of the HM Land Registry portal can search for user accounts under 'Administrative services' > 'Manage users' by User ID, name, common identity group, or account type or role, then update details and log out.

Lodge a unilateral notice (e-UN1) via the HM Land Registry portal by entering the title number, checking limitations, completing applicant, notice and evidence details, then submitting and paying the fee.

Log in to the HM Land Registry portal, go to Administrative services > Manage groups, find and select the group, then choose View, Update or Delete to change its address, contact details or correspondence email, and log out when finished.

The HM Land Registry portal's "Services Requested" page lets users view services ordered on their Variable Direct Debit accounts over the past 7 days, with daily totals, sorting options, and a description breakdown.

Ratings and Other Ranks in the Ministry of Defence can claim a backdated annual laundry Flat Rate Expense Allowance (£80 Royal Navy, £100 Army, Royal Marines and RAF), applied through a tax code adjustment, or actual laundry expenses via HMRC.

The Electronic Communications Code, reformed by the Digital Economy Act 2017 (Schedule 3A to the Communications Act 2003), governs relationships between site providers and telecoms network operators, with Ofcom issuing supporting guidance and Tribunal resolution available for disputes.

Legislation passed in November 2017 lets charitable companies convert to CIOs under a phased timetable from 1 January 2018, requires all CIOs to be listed on Companies House's Index of Company Names, and sets rules for name approval.

Victims' services are shifting from national government provision to local commissioning by Police and Crime Commissioners, with funding extended for homicide and peer support services until 30 September 2014, while the Victims' Code is now in force and capacity-building support is offered to voluntary sector bidders.

Everyone needing access to non-public areas of the 2012 London Olympic and Paralympic venues had to be accredited by LOCOG, with the Home Office conducting background checks (including criminal record checks, where unspent convictions generally mattered) and the Olympic Clearing House deleting case files in January 2013.

Land managers have a legal duty to prevent waste harming the environment, covering hazardous and non-hazardous waste handling, registration for carriers, permits or exemptions for treatment and disposal, fly-tipping responsibilities, and a ban on burning stubble.

Companies House credit account holders can switch from postal invoices to eBilling, registering with their name, email, password and latest invoice details, and unlock locked accounts by emailing their 8-digit account number, which is unlocked within 24 hours.

Local authorities are encouraged to map publicly owned assets such as ducts, fibre, buildings, CCTV, and streetlights, ideally in a shared database, to help operators plan and deploy fixed and mobile networks.

The page sets out Ministry of Defence decisions on alleged human rights breaches (Articles 2 and 3 ECHR) arising from UK operations in Iraq during Operation Telic, with summary decisions and reasons published as downloadable PDFs in English and Arabic.

Regulated businesses must appoint a nominated officer within the business to receive and report suspicious activity to the NCA, arrange cover during absences, and train all staff, including front-line employees, on money laundering laws, procedures, and penalties, keeping training records.

When you move from Housing Benefit to Universal Credit, your Housing Benefit continues for 2 extra weeks automatically, without repayment, to cover housing costs until your first monthly Universal Credit payment.

The Mutuals Partnership Support Programme was a pilot that tested how mutuals can collaborate to bid for wider, integrated public service contracts, supporting three projects in housing, health and social care.

Food products must carry a legal, customary, or descriptive name that isn't misleading, with reserved names used only when conditions are met, ingredient differences and treatments such as freezing or irradiation disclosed near the name.

The National Conversation on Health Inequalities page shares video photo stories from Public Health England showing how housing, employment, education and community projects tackle health inequalities and improve wellbeing.

The page presents the South West England region of the National Geological Screening for a geological disposal facility (GDF), divided into four subregions with broadly similar geology, stating that no specific site has been identified and any future decision would require community agreement and consents. (Count: about 35 words, so trimming needed.)

Revised to at most 30 words:

The page divides South West England into four geologically similar subregions for the National Geological Screening for a GDF, stressing that no specific site has been identified.

Electricity licence holders can seek permission to install and keep power lines on private land, either by voluntary agreement or, if that fails, through a compulsory necessary wayleave or Compulsory Purchase Order under the Electricity Act 1989, with fees, hearings and application timelines set out.

Necrotising fasciitis is a rare but serious bacterial infection of soft tissue and fascia, often entering through a cut or surgery, with early signs of severe pain and fever that can progress rapidly to death without prompt treatment with intravenous antibiotics and sometimes surgery.

NHS Injury Cost Recovery charges rise from 1 April 2020 by 2.4% (HCHS inflation), applying only to injuries sustained on or after that date: ambulance £224, non-admitted treatment £743, daily in-patient £913, maximum £54,566.

NHS England's population screening programmes collect and analyse quality data, including quarterly key performance indicator reports, and set national standards to reduce variation and keep local services safe and effective.

Northern England Subregion 5 is a technical screening area where geology may suit a geological disposal facility (GDF), with clay-rich and rock salt layers under most of it, though no specific site has been identified and any decision would need community agreement and consents.

The GOV.UK page provides the revised (August 2019) Notice of Rights and Entitlements, which sets out a person's rights while in police detention, and offers it in English, easy read, and many other languages.

Councils must investigate smell complaints from industrial, trade, and business premises that amount to a statutory nuisance, meaning they unreasonably interfere with enjoyment of premises or harm health, and can issue abatement notices requiring the smell to be stopped or restricted.

Guidance for applying for consent to build or vary onshore electricity power stations in England and Wales, explaining which body decides applications (the Secretary of State, Planning Inspectorate, local planning authorities or devolved governments), plus environmental, carbon capture and CHP requirements.

Following an objection to a UK trade mark examination, you can request a hearing if you think your application was unfairly handled or disagree with the decision, or file evidence of distinctiveness (such as use, turnover and promotion) in a witness statement, seek consent letters from earlier rights holders, divide the application, or request an extension of time.

Pigeon paramyxovirus mainly infects pigeons, not humans, and must be reported immediately to Defra, Welsh, or Scottish authorities if suspected, since it is a notifiable disease that can spread to chickens and cause Newcastle disease.

Withdrawn Parole Board guide (last amended August 2018) for members on oral hearings, covering pre-hearing issues, roles, procedure, decisions, and equal treatment, now superseded by January 2025 guidance.

Employers can often skip deducting tax from harvest workers and casual beaters employed for two weeks or less (or one day or less with no further contract), but must still keep records, report pay, and deduct National Insurance where earnings exceed the thresholds, while the pay remains taxable.

Landlords living abroad for over six months a year must pay UK tax on rental income, collected through the Non-resident Landlord Scheme by letting agents or tenants paying over £100 a week, who must register, deduct basic-rate tax, pay HMRC quarterly and file annual reports.

Pennines subregion 1 screening: suitable geology for a geological disposal facility may exist in parts, with strong granites and slates, but their properties are unconfirmed, and past lead and fluorite mining plus possible future exploration add concerns, though no site has been identified.

Subregion 4 (Pennines and adjacent areas) is a technical screening area where a geological disposal facility may be feasible in most of its extent, mainly within clay-rich and rock salt layers, though no specific site has been identified and further study and community agreement would be required.

Pension administrators can use HMRC's GMP checker, via Pension Scheme Online with a Government Gateway login, to get instant or bulk Guaranteed Minimum Pension calculations for members, requiring their scheme contracted-out number, National Insurance number, and name.

Lump sum death benefits from pension schemes are taxable if the member died aged 75 or over or the payment isn't made within 2 years of the scheme learning of the death, with tax deducted via PAYE for trivial commutation payments, Income Tax on payments to individuals, or the special lump sum death benefits charge otherwise.

Trustees are the legal owners of a pension scheme's assets and must act in members' best interests, impartially, prudently, responsibly and honestly, keep HMRC and member records, invest the assets, ensure adequate funding, and report to The Pensions Regulator.

Pension scheme investments face tax conditions on loans, shares, borrowing and transactions with members, employers or connected parties, with extra rules for investment-regulated schemes, and breaches trigger tax charges for the scheme administrator and, usually, the member or employer.

The page provides resources and training for health professionals and commissioners supporting the pertussis (whooping cough) vaccination programme for pregnant women, which JCVI advised continuing until at least June 2019.

This GOV.UK page explains that pests and diseases harm fruit and vegetable production, urges growers to recognise early signs and report to the Plant Health and Seeds Inspectorate, and outlines Defra's role in plant health.

The PACS programme in India, initiated in 2001 and run by the UK's Department for International Development, built the capacity of civil society organisations in India's poorest districts, helping over six million poor people claim entitlements worth more than £125 million.
APHA inspects every poultry farm using specialist marketing terms like 'free range' at least once per flock turnaround, checking facilities, records and procedures, usually without advance notice.

Natural England's pre-submission screening service offers paid advice (£110 per hour) on whether planning proposals affecting protected species are likely to meet licensing requirements, including a review of draft application documents, a written advice note, an optional site visit, and follow-up support before formal submission.

Pregnant women should avoid close contact with livestock giving birth, such as helping ewes lamb or handling afterbirth and contaminated bedding, because infections like chlamydiosis, listeriosis, Q fever and toxoplasmosis can harm mother and baby.

Set up in 2016 to build on the Recall Review Steering Group and Lynn Faulds Wood's review, the GOV.UK Working Group on Product Recalls and Safety, chaired by Neil Gibbins, brings together fire, trading standards, consumer and industry experts to improve product recall and white goods safety.

The UK government welcomed the 2016 House of Lords report on sexual violence in conflict, responded in June 2016 with PSVI progress and priorities, and committed to working with Parliament, including a new All Party Parliamentary Group.

Libraries within a library authority's statutory public service fall under the PLR scheme, with loan data collected from a rotating representative sample of authorities to calculate author payments, while libraries wholly outside that service need no PLR agreements.

Highway authorities must record and maintain public rights of way, keep them open and free of obstructions, improve accessibility of structures such as stiles and gates, consider biodiversity and disabled users, review rights of way improvement plans every 10 years, and protect historical pre-1949 routes.

Public sector bodies can safely use public cloud for sensitive data, but each organisation must make its own risk-based decision, understand the shared security responsibility with providers, and follow vendor and NCSC security guidance.

Virtual school heads manage pupil premium and early years pupil premium funding for their local authority's looked-after children, allocating it to schools and early years providers, ensuring it supports personal education plans, returning unspent funds to DfE, and reporting to Ofsted on its impact.
Travellers to the February 2018 Pyeongchang Winter Olympics and Paralympics should book accommodation and transport early, as Pyeongchang lodging will be limited and venue access strictly controlled.

Financial services workers and energy companies penalised by regulators such as the FCA, PRA, Pensions Regulator, Bank of England, Ofgem or NIAUR can refer the decision to the Upper Tribunal, by submitting a form and explaining why the decision was wrong.

To join the intensive care quality improvement programme (ICCQIP), a hospital must email the ICCQIP team to nominate a local administrator, who then completes online training, registers on the ICU data capture system, and signs up data entry users.

Guidance for DfE Chromebooks ordered before October 2021 explains how to remove Cisco Umbrella content filtering via the Google Admin console, after its licences were extended to 30 September 2022, and warns that schools must then provide alternative safety software.

Results-based financing (RBF) provides incentive payments, made only after independently verified outputs, to businesses delivering low-carbon off-grid energy products such as solar lamps, cookstoves and mini-grids across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

Rift Valley fever, a mosquito-spread notifiable disease that has never been found in Great Britain, affects sheep, goats, cattle and humans, and must be reported immediately to Defra, the Welsh contact or the local Scottish Field Services Office if suspected.

Government assesses UK emergency risks annually through a confidential National Risk Assessment and public National Risk Register, while local resilience forums produce Community Risk Registers tailored to each area's specific hazards.
This GOV.UK tariff quota notice sets out new 0% duty quotas for sausages (excluding wild boar) and fresh, chilled or frozen pig meat originating from Iceland, running from 1 May to 31 December 2018.

Fill in a community buildings schedule spreadsheet (name, address line, postcode, tax year end and small donation totals up to 500 lines), using the correct ODF version for your software, then attach it to your Charities Online GASDS claim.

Gov.uk's school resource management checklist offers tools for checking school efficiency, benchmarking spending and staffing, planning finances and workforce, finding approved suppliers, submitting SVFS forms, and accessing financial advice and training.

Guidance for setting up Google Chromebooks from the Get help with technology programme or donations covers enrolling devices in the Google Admin console, content filtering responsibilities, and built-in software security features.

The page describes a national screening study finding that most of South West England Subregion 1 may have suitable geology for a geological disposal facility (GDF), with clay and salt layers possibly suitable, though no specific site has been identified and further work is needed.

Our screening of South West England Subregion 2 suggests a suitable geological setting for a geological disposal facility may exist across most of the area, though no specific site has been identified, mining and oil and gas exploration need monitoring, and any decision would require community agreement and consents.

You can ask HMRC's Stamp Office for an informal opinion on how much Stamp Duty, penalties or interest are due, or whether relief or exemption applies, by emailing them before or after a transfer, and request a formal opinion if you strongly disagree.

Some property transactions are exempt from Stamp Duty Land Tax and need no HMRC return, including transfers with no chargeable consideration, inherited property, divorce settlements, and low-value freehold or short-lease deals, while Scotland and Wales use different taxes.
Stamp Duty rates for freehold and leasehold land transfers from 28 March 2000 to 30 November 2003 are set out, with SDLT applying from 1 December 2003 instead.

GOV.UK explains when paperless transfers of shares and securities are exempt from or qualify for Stamp Duty Reserve Tax relief, covering gifts, inheritances, divorce, intra-group and charity transfers, and how to claim them via CREST flags or HMRC stamping.

Statutory Adoption Pay eligibility and calculation vary by employment type, including agency and casual workers, agricultural workers, mariners, NHS staff, supply teachers, company directors (depending on how and when they are paid), employees with multiple jobs, and those working abroad.

Statutory Pay is a legal entitlement that must be paid in full and clearly identified (e.g. as SSP or SMP) in any Compromise Agreement, with tax and NICs deducted, rather than being folded into a general settlement figure.

Businesses registered for Air Passenger Duty can apply to file annual returns by writing to HMRC's Central Assurance Team with their registration details and expected liability, with reapplication needed if annual returns were stopped within the previous 12 months.

The British Embassy Hanoi invites partners to submit proposals for projects in Vietnam backing UK priorities, with funding up to £60,000 across themes such as smart cities, media, education technology, and healthcare, plus the Prosperity Fund.
Patents Court guidance explains how to bring a complex patent or registered design dispute in London's Rolls Building, covering claim fees, serving documents, case management, hearings, and appeals.

Tax agents need formal authorisation to deal with HMRC for clients, and if none exists during a compliance check, the client can use form Comp1 to grant temporary authorisation limited to that check, sent to the HMRC officer handling it.
HMRC warns NHS workers returning during the COVID-19 outbreak to beware of tax avoidance schemes, often run through umbrella companies, that disguise true earnings as non-taxable loans or advances.

HMRC may require a deposit or bond (a security) from those at risk of not paying tax or duty on time, set out in a Notice of Requirement, which they can use to settle unpaid bills, with rules varying by tax type on how long it's held, how to dispute it, and penalties for not providing it.
If a company fails to deduct PAYE from a director's pay and later pays the tax itself, the director is taxed on that amount unless they make it good, subject to exemptions.

Payments for using celebrities' or sportspeople's image rights are taxed as professional income if self-employed, as earnings under PAYE if made for employment duties, and as company profits (with shareholder or director rewards taxed normally) if paid to a UK image rights company.

Employees of trading organisations generally cannot deduct entertaining expenses, though reasonable costs of genuine business occasions may be exempt for employees, while non-trading employees such as civil servants can claim entertainment costs incurred wholly, exclusively and necessarily in their duties.

Template legal documents, created by Bates Wells Braithwaite with the DCMS Mutuals Team, to help local authorities and mutuals spin out public services, covering transfer, funding, services, back-office, lease and licence agreements, though they are starting points only and not legal advice.

Battle Back is an MOD-led adaptive sport and adventurous training programme, delivered with Help for Heroes and The Royal British Legion, that helps wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans recover confidence, independence and wellbeing.

The Fast Track Digital Workforce Fund is a £3 million DCMS pilot, co-run with Manchester Combined Authority and Lancashire LEP, that funded employer-led consortia to deliver digital skills training for low-paid workers; the fund is now closed.

Ken Thomson, Scottish Government Director General, shares why the Civil Service Leadership Academy matters: it helps leaders improve, support Ministers and citizens better, and reflect on their own growth.

The Trade Advocacy Fund helps the poorest and most vulnerable countries, including some lower middle income nations, prepare for and take part in trade negotiations through expert advice, negotiator training, and logistical support.

Independent trade unions seeking recognition from employers with at least 21 workers must first request recognition in writing, then apply to the Central Arbitration Committee if refused or unanswered, which proceeds through acceptance, bargaining unit, access, balloting, and bargaining machinery stages.

Transport document guidance explains that non-hazardous goods use a Standard Shipping Note (SSN), hazardous goods require a Dangerous Goods Note (DGN) or declaration, and exporters may use an Export Cargo Shipping Instruction (ECSI) to give forwarders or carriers handling instructions.

UKHSA no longer publishes tuberculosis country data, so users are directed to the WHO Global TB Programme website and its mobile app for current TB incidence rates, which are used to decide BCG vaccination and new-entrant testing eligibility.

Fertilisers made from processed animal by-products must be stored away from animal feed and inaccessible to livestock, can't be used as feed, and carry grazing and harvested-herbage restrictions (2 months for pigs, 21 days for other farmed animals), with some unprocessed by-products exempt and detailed record-keeping required.

The Capital Goods Scheme lets UK businesses spread the VAT reclaimed on expensive assets, such as land and buildings (£250,000+), computers (£50,000+) and vessels (£50,000+), over several years, with adjustments if taxable use changes.

HMRC offers written VAT clearance for uncertain transactions, and until 30 September 2018 it trialled VAT rulings for complex cross-border transactions involving two or more participating EU member states.

Goods lost, stolen, damaged or destroyed: VAT depends on whether you supplied them, who was responsible for them, and whether you issued a VAT invoice, with rules for losses in transit, theft, fraud and insurance claims.

Eligibility for the Victims of Overseas Terrorism Compensation Scheme requires meeting nationality rules (British, armed forces, or EU/EEA/Swiss nationals or their family members) and ordinary UK residence for three years before the act, with evidence such as passports and documents showing a UK address.

Wales Subregion 3 is a GDF screening area where no suitable site has been identified, with suitable rock likely insufficient for all the waste, mining, oil, gas and coal licence areas, and thermal springs at Taffs Well needing consideration.

Wales Subregion 4 is a GDF screening area offshore-inshore where clay-rich rock layers and, in the southern half, rock salt may host a facility, though no specific site has been identified and further study is needed.

Wales Subregion 5 is a GDF screening area where slates and similar strong rocks may suit a repository at depth, though lack of deep data, past mining, and offshore oil and gas exploration need further work, and no specific site has been identified.

Veterans with an existing War Pension can claim for an additional condition caused or worsened by pre-6 April 2005 armed forces service using form WPS0002, with payment normally starting from the date the new claim is received.

A 3-part payment is a single, consistent payment approach for urgent and emergency care networks, combining a guaranteed core payment for capacity, a volume-based payment for patient needs met, and a payment linked to network-wide outcomes and performance.

Multilateral gain/loss sharing is a financial mechanism in which providers and commissioners in a local care economy pool the difference between expected and actual spending, then distribute these gains or losses across the network to support integrated care.

Where an employee has more than one job with you, or with an employer you carry on business in association with, you may need to aggregate their earnings to calculate National Insurance contributions, unless HMRC accepts it isn't reasonably practicable; PAYE tax is unaffected.

Employees can set up Direct Collection or Direct Payment schemes with HMRC by phone or post to pay Class 1 National Insurance when no PAYE Income Tax or employer NICs are due, and employers report such earnings on Full Payment Summaries with zeros in taxable pay fields and code NT.

Developers and network operators should share information early, through agreements with trade bodies and individual developers, to deliver gigabit-capable connections to new homes, which the government is considering backing with new backstop measures.

Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne viral disease endemic in tropical Africa and South America, with recent large outbreaks in Brazil, Nigeria and Angola; unvaccinated travellers are advised to get vaccinated and take bite-avoidance precautions.
